chapter: War years, Decca records and La Conga
title: Plans for Marcelino Guerra and Varona's unreliability
summary: From the army Machito said to put Guerra in his place; Mario formed Guerra's group, called the Second Afro-Cubans.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Well, in that particular time, I was in the Army. When Mario told me that Marcelino Guerra was coming to New York, I said: put Marcelino in my place because I have a

great respect as a artist, because he is a fine artist, and fine composer and if you were recording his numbers, and he is a great singer, I said: Mario, why don't you put Marcelino Guerra in the band? But Polito Galindez was working with Curbelo and when Curbelo get another singer, so Mario took Polito Galindez and he organized Marcelino Guerra's band, that we used to call it "Second Afro-Cubans"," Marcelino Guerra and "Second Afro-Cubans" because Varona was the pianist from our band, but he was young and was kind of unreliable and we had a lot of shows to play, like Carmen Amaya, Argentinita, all those big artists from Spain and we need a legitimate piano player and Varona was - so to us Barona was a great asset. So in that particular time .....
